Out of curiosity, since this bit is running in a controller, how is this flag going to be evaulated? i.e. what is `openfeature.NewDefaultClient().Boolean()` doing exactly?

Oh, that’s a good find. I missed the fact that this code isn’t instrumented with our OF components that populate the evaluation context with the required data.

What openfeature.NewDefaultClient().Boolean() does depends on the configuration. In a nutshell, it evaluates the feature flag through the configured provider.

The provider can either use remote evaluation or a wired static configuration that is interoperable with the old feature toggles manager.

With the static provider, the behavior is the same as before: provisioningExport=true in the config means the feature is enabled.

Remote evaluation, on the other hand, sends a request over the network to the MTFF service, passing along the evaluation context, and expects the flag to be defined in the dedicated [goff section](https://github.com/grafana/deployment_tools/tree/master/ksonnet/environments/hosted-grafana/waves/feature-toggles/goff/app-platform) in deployment tools.

Since we’re using a single namespace here without any additional evaluation context, the result depends on the rollout percentage and the key. In practice, this means flag evaluation will be consistent across requests using the same namespace.

To make things clear in my slow mind 😆 

For MT controllers, since we have `[feature_toggles] provisioningExport = true` there (see e.g. https://github.com/grafana/kube-manifests/blob/master/flux/dev-us-central-0/grafana-apps/ConfigMap-provisioning-jobqueue-operator.yaml#L12 - which contains the `.ini` configuration for the interested controller) this means that the bit:

```go
evalCtx := features.EvaluationContextFromTargetingKey(cfg.Namespace)
enabled := openfeature.NewDefaultClient().Boolean(ctx, featuremgmt.FlagProvisioningExport, false, evalCtx)
```

would **always** evaluate to true, no matter the `cfg.Namespace` passed, am I right?

Yes, this is correct. [RunTargetServer:L134-138](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/pkg/server/bootstrap/servers.go#L134-L138) configures OF provider to use the static one that reads flags from config.ini. The flag will always be resolved to true regardless of the namespace. We still need to pass a namespace (or any key) though as open feature will fail if targeting key is missing.

In general, targeting key comes in handy when you plan for canary releases or gradual rollouts. But you'll need to configure remote provider for that purpose.

### Cleanup can delete live documents **Medium Severity** Expired-trash cleanup searches, then deletes by document id with no check that the hit is still trash. Live and deleted objects share the same `SearchID`, so a recreate that is indexed between the search and `Batch` can have the new live document removed from the index. Search then misses that object until a rebuild.
Additional Locations (1) - [`pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go#L1834-L1840`](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/ed7a2ff656b75794698f10728e46722938c56516/pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go#L1834-L1840)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit ed7a2ff656b75794698f10728e46722938c56516. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

Real, but we are accepting it. Closing the race means serialising index writes with a lock, and index updates happen on the query path (`UpdateIndex` -> `BulkIndex`), so queries would end up waiting behind cleanup batches. The window is a few milliseconds, on trash that has already sat in the index for the whole retention period, and the document comes back on the next rebuild. Written down in the comment on `removeExpiredTrash`.

### Origin ignores auto-sync feature flag **Medium Severity** `setExtraConfigOrigin` marks a staged config as `auto-sync` when its identifier matches the configured external Alertmanager UID, without checking whether `alerting.syncExternalAlertmanager` is enabled. The sync worker returns immediately when that flag is off, so it will not rewrite the extra config. Callers that treat `managed_by` as current ownership would then hide Revert on a leftover staged config the user can actually remove, which is the same stuck state this field is meant to prevent after a flag rollback.

When an existing installation upgrades, these assignments run only for resources that are subsequently reindexed, but this change leaves both `IndexAffectingHash` and the required index features unchanged. I checked `getIndexMaxAge` and `shouldRebuildIndex`: non-dashboard indexes default to no age-based rebuild (`max_file_index_age = 0`), so unchanged notebooks, playlists, folders, and similar resources can remain without tags or descriptions indefinitely, producing silently incomplete filtering, facets, and text results after rollout. Good catch on the diagnosis — this is real, and it matches what the description already flags: existing indexes keep documents written before the change, and non-dashboard kinds have `max_file_index_age = 0`, so they never age out on their own.

On the remedy, though, I don't think adding a rebuild trigger belongs in this PR. There are only two, and neither fits:

**`IndexAffectingHash` can't reach the affected kinds.** It returns `""` for any group/resource absent from `mapProvider.fields`, which only holds kinds with manifest-declared `searchFields` — repo-wide that's `apps/dashboard`, `apps/iam` and `apps/alerting/rules`. **An `IndexFeature` in `requiredIndexFeatures` contradicts its own documented bar:**

Missing tags/description makes results *incomplete* (fewer hits, thinner facets), not *wrong*. That slice is currently empty, so this would be the first entry ever added, and it gates index use — every index in every tenant would be unusable until it rebuilt. That's a large operational event relative to the problem.

The mechanism that does fit is **`min_file_index_build_version`**, bumped to the release carrying this change: asynchronous, doesn't gate index use, and it's the existing operator knob for exactly this ("index was built with older Grafana, it will be rebuilt asynchronously"). Individual resources also pick the fields up on their next write in the meantime.

I've updated the description to propose that explicitly rather than leaving the trigger as an open question. Flagging @pstibrany to confirm it gets bumped for this release — happy to be told otherwise if there's a preferred mechanism I've missed.

I would leave this out for now for multiple reasons:
* dashboards have their description indexed already
* no other resources search for description today
* most on-prem users don't even have on-disk indexed, but use in-memory indexes -- they are rebuilt on each restart
* in our cloud setup we already trigger regular rebuilds

I'm fine bumping `min_file_index_build_version` for next minor release to make sure we don't hit problems for file-based indexes, but it doesn't seem urgent for now.

### Contains match case sensitivity mismatch **Medium Severity** `contains` filtering is case-sensitive in the memory store via `strings.Contains`, but case-insensitive in Postgres via `ILIKE`. The PR aims to match legacy tag search, which is case-insensitive, so the same query can return different results depending on the store backend.
Additional Locations (1) - [`pkg/registry/apps/annotation/postgres_tags.go#L102-L106`](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/b1adbce31c5ac09492a043838aa00b32cc6ec00c/pkg/registry/apps/annotation/postgres_tags.go#L102-L106)

### Contains treats LIKE wildcards literally elsewhere **Medium Severity** `contains` is described as substring match, but the Postgres path builds an `ILIKE` pattern from the raw query value without escaping `%` or `_`. Those characters act as wildcards in SQL, while the memory store uses literal `strings.Contains`, so the same request can return different tags depending on the backend—especially for common underscore-containing tag names.
Additional Locations (1) - [`pkg/registry/apps/annotation/memory_store.go#L258-L262`](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/b56f66232811fc42b03216f0252cfb9f3d46d664/pkg/registry/apps/annotation/memory_store.go#L258-L262)

### Contains wildcards leak via sql adapter **Medium Severity** `contains` is passed straight into the legacy `Tag` filter, which still treats `_` and `%` as `LIKE`/`ILIKE` wildcards. Postgres and memory stores, plus the new handler tests, treat those characters as literals. On the sql-adapter backend, searches like `contains=_a` can match unintended tags such as `servicexb`.
